method: Geometry first, from prims.pkl (area 'ground'). 1) Rendered the part overview (grid 1, inserts) and context views: the whole ground floor, the pool side, the upper floor above the north room and the elevation sheet. The elevations were not used to decide kinds. 2) Extracted the wall-layer segments and paired facing wall-end closing segments along each wall line (gaps.py) to get candidate gaps. Then clustered every DOOR/D-JAMB/WIN/WALL-GL/DSYM item (symbols.py) and every arc of radius > 0.3 m on any layer (arcs.py) and accounted for each cluster. This also catches door symbols on layer 0, on WALL and in xref blocks. 3) Checked all 16 zoomed 6x6 m tiles (grid 0.5, inserts): x 31-37, 37-43, 43-49, 48.5-54.5 by y 5-11, 11-17, 17-23, 20.2-26.2. Then made close zooms (grid 0.1-0.25) for the bathroom door and pocket door, the dining/hall gap, the north-room west and north sides, the corridor and closets, the glass foyer door, the ramp landing and steps, the NE room and the SE gates. 4) Took a and b from wall-end closing lines, column faces, jamb inserts and frame boxes, on the centre line of the host wall. Checked each gap with an intersection query for wall lines running across it: only an untrimmed wall at GE-11, a room-outline polyline at GE-05, and grid lines. 5) Rendered the part with a marker at every opening centre (overview plus two zooms of the west block); no gap, swing, leaf, jamb pair or glazing was left unmarked. Result: 18 openings (12 doors incl. 2 site gates, 4 windows... see kinds), 4 glass-wall segments, plus uncertain and rejected cases.
